tools.name: config_prune
tools.description: Remove dead weight from the local config file at ~/.config/rediacc/<config>.json. Three buckets are cleaned, all pure-local (no SSH/renet calls): (1) ACME cert-cache entries whose anchor GUID/repo/machine is no longer in the active config; (2) archived repositories whose grace period has expired (default 7 days, see defaults.pruneGraceDays); (3) dangling cross-references (machine→strategy, strategy→repo). Resources still in use, credentials, storage tokens, and known-hosts are never touched. Default behavior is to apply changes; pass --dry-run to preview only.

dry_run.description: Preview what would be removed without modifying the config file. Mirrors the default-off semantics of the other prune commands.

certs_only.description: Restrict to the ACME cert-cache bucket. Skips archive purging and cross-reference cleanup. Mutually exclusive with --archives-only and --refs-only.

archives_only.description: Restrict to expired-archive purging. Skips cert-cache and cross-reference cleanup. Mutually exclusive with --certs-only and --refs-only.

refs_only.description: Restrict to dangling cross-references (machine→strategy, strategy→repo excludes/includes). Skips cert-cache and archives. Mutually exclusive with --certs-only and --archives-only.

orphan_repos.description: Remove repository entries that are placed on no machine. Each entry holds that repo's credential and SSH key, so this is unrecoverable. Run 'rdc config reconcile' first so placement reflects the machines.

gone_machine_repos.description: Archive repository entries placed on a machine that is no longer in the config. Archived, not dropped: each keeps its credential and is restorable until the archive grace expires. Selects only this bucket: the cert-cache, archive and cross-reference buckets are skipped unless their own --*-only flag is also given.

grace_days.description: Override the archive grace window (in days) for this invocation. Falls back to defaults.pruneGraceDays in the config, then to 7 if neither is set.

tools.name: machine_prune
tools.description: Remove orphaned datastore resources and stale snapshots from a machine. The base run cleans renet-internal datastore artifacts (BTRFS subvolumes, lock files, tmpfiles). The optional flags below enable progressively narrower repo cleanups: --orphaned-repos uses the local CLI config as the only signal, while --prune-unknown additionally consults the renet .interim/state mirror so legitimate forks created by other tools survive even when missing from the local config. Both deletion paths run a mount-safety preflight; pass --force-delete-mounted to override. Returns the result, or a job id when the run outlasts about 20 s (follow it with job_status or job_logs).

dry_run.description: Show what would be removed without making changes

orphaned_repos.description: Delete every repo image on the machine that is not in your local CLI config. Coarse: it also removes forks created by other tools that have no local config entry, even when their renet mirror correctly identifies them as forks. Use --prune-unknown for the narrower behavior that respects the mirror.

prune_unknown.description: Delete only repos the renet .interim/state mirror cannot classify (not in local config AND no fork-marked mirror). Strictly narrower than --orphaned-repos: forks-without-config are preserved when the mirror identifies them. Pre-mirror legacy orphans and stale grands whose config entry was deleted both fall in this bucket.

force_delete_mounted.description: Override the mount-safety preflight and delete repos even if they are currently mounted or have running Docker containers. Distinct from --force (which only overrides the archive grace period). Applies to both --orphaned-repos and --prune-unknown.

The commit refuses to mount; check it out to get a writable copy. Returns the result, or a job id when the run outlasts about 20 s (follow it with job_status or job_logs).

tools.name: repo_delete
tools.description: Delete a repository and its data. A fork's config entry moves to deletedRepositories, which frees the name and keeps the GUID restorable via 'repo admin archive restore'; a grand repo's entry, or one pushed to other machines, is kept unless --archive-config is passed. Takes a positional <ref>; a bare name resolves to the grand line and is refused when several repos share the base name, so pass name:tag to target a fork. Returns the result, or a job id when the run outlasts about 20 s (follow it with job_status or job_logs).

ref.description: Repository ref: name, or name:tag, optionally with @machine (for example shop or shop:test)

archive_config.description: Move config entry to deletedRepositories for later recovery

purge_backups.description: Also delete the repository's cloud backups now, instead of letting them expire

tools.name: repo_diff
tools.description: Git-style file-level diff between two copy-on-write forked repositories. Reports Added, Modified, Deleted, and Renamed files. Diffs the repository given by the positional <ref> (the target / new side) against its parent, resolved from local config, or against an explicit --base repository (the base / old side). Metadata-only and size-independent: it diffs the encrypted LUKS images at the block level without decrypting them, so a 1 GB repo and a 100 GB repo diff in the same milliseconds. Returns the result, or a job id when the run outlasts about 20 s (follow it with job_status or job_logs).

ref.description: Repository ref: name, or name:tag, optionally with @machine (for example shop or shop:test)

base.description: Repository to diff against (the base / old side); defaults to the parent of <ref>

name_only.description: Print only changed file paths, one per line (no status letters)

stat.description: Show per-file change magnitude (byte and block deltas) and totals

content.description: Show a unified text diff for a single file (requires a file path)

fast.description: Trust the block filter; skip content-hash confirmation (may over-report Modified)

tools.name: repo_fork
tools.description: Create a near-instant CoW fork of a repository with a NEW GUID and networkId (fully independent copy). FORK IS CONSTANT-TIME regardless of repo size: BTRFS reflink clones the image so 100 GB and 1 GB repos fork in the same ~seconds, never proportional to repo size. Fork shares the parent name with a different tag (name:tag model, like Docker images). Online forking supported (parent can stay running). Fork gets new auto-route domain. After fork, deploy with repo_up. Fork-of-fork allowed (same base name, different tag). CROSS-MACHINE: fork locally first, then use repo_push to transfer fork to target machine, then repo_up on target. Returns the result, or a job id when the run outlasts about 20 s (follow it with job_status or job_logs).

ref.description: Repository ref: name, or name:tag, optionally with @machine (for example shop or shop:test)

checkpoint.description: Create CRIU checkpoint on source before forking (capture process memory state for restore on fork)

immutable.description: Mark the fork read-only: it refuses to mount, keeping its image byte-stable forever (a frozen commit/base for cross-machine delta push)

up.description: Mount and start services after forking (fork + mount + up in one command)

no_wait.description: With --up: return once containers are started; health checks continue in the background (ideal for throwaway forks)

tools.name: repo_merge
tools.description: Lifecycle-safe merge of a source commit/fork into a target working fork. Refuses a mounted/running target unless --force (which quiesces it first); never mutates a live mount; builds the result in a reflink clone and atomically swaps it in. Returns the result, or a job id when the run outlasts about 20 s (follow it with job_status or job_logs).

resolve.description: Per-file conflict resolution for a three-way merge: 'ours' keeps the target's version, 'theirs' takes the source's. Omit for whole-image fast-forward (take-theirs).

base.description: Common-ancestor commit GUID for a three-way merge (used with --resolve). Defaults to the source commit's parent or the target's current commit.

tools.name: repo_migrate
tools.description: Move a repository to another machine with minimal downtime: a two-phase copy (bulk sync while running, then a short stop + delta sync + start on the destination) with DNS cutover. The repo keeps its identity and secrets. Use repo_push for a backup copy that stays on both machines. Returns the result, or a job id when the run outlasts about 20 s (follow it with job_status or job_logs).
